title: S&P 500 Breaks Bearish Wedge | Investing.com
text:
S&P 500 Breaks Bearish Wedge By Faraday Research (Matthew Weller) Stock Markets 5 hours ago (Jan 22, 2019 03:24PM ET) www.investing.com/analysis/sp-500-breaks-bearish-wedge-traders-monitoring-earnings-and-shutdown-shenanigans-200378058 S&P 500 Breaks Bearish Wedge By Faraday Research (Matthew Weller) | 5 hours ago (Jan 22, 2019 03:24PM ET) This article has already been saved in your Saved Items Follow
US stock markets were closed Monday in remembrance of Dr. Martin Luther King and given the headwinds the world economy faces, perhaps policymakers could benefit from his overriding message of inclusion and cooperation..
Traders are aggressively selling US equities, with major indices unwinding the gains from Friday’s trade-optimism-induced rally. From a technical perspective, the S&P 500 has now broken down from its “rising wedge” pattern off the Boxing Day panic low. Despite the seemingly bullish name, this price action pattern shows that buyers are struggling to push the price higher on each subsequent swing. It is a classic sign of waning buying pressure and often portends a bearish reversal. That said, we’re hesitant to make any broad conclusions off merely a single down day, especially following such a strong rally off the lows.
Moving forward, bulls will want to see if prices can hold above the key previous support level in the 2600 range. A break below there could open the door for a retest of the late December lows. Meanwhile, the key area to watch if prices rally will be the confluence of the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement of the Q4 swoon and the 100-day moving average near 2715. Daily S&P 500
Source: TradingView, FOREX.com
Shutdown tensions are poised to pick up with 800,000 government employees set to miss their second paycheck on Friday, and three of four largest publicly-traded companies on the planet set to report Q4 earnings next week ( AAPL , MSFT , AMZN ), volatility may be here to stay.
